title: customers.measurement-version-confirmed.v1
description: A customer's measurements were confirmed against a template version. Published in the same transaction as the version, its values and the consumption of the draft they came from (docs/architecture/invariants.md section 4.3). It carries NO measurement — not one number, not the field keys, not how many there were: measurements are sensitive personal data under docs/nfr/data-classification.md, and an outbox row fans out to every registered handler and is retained, so a payload carrying them would be a second uncontrolled copy in a table nobody thinks of as holding measurements. A consumer that needs the values reads them through the module's own contract, which re-authorises and audits the read. It also does not mean 're-measure anything': a garment job snapshots the version it was confirmed against and does not move when a newer one appears (INV-JOB-01).
$comment: additionalProperties is true on purpose. conventions.md section 5.5 permits additive changes within a major version, so a subscriber must tolerate a field it has not seen; a closed schema would make every such addition breaking. required lists the fields present when v1 was published — a field added within v1 is optional forever, because a dead-lettered message replayed later carries the payload as it was written.

eventId.description: Identity of this occurrence. Delivery is at least once; consumers de-duplicate on it.

occurredAt.description: When the measurements were confirmed, in UTC.

aggregateId.description: The measurement version. What a garment job pins, and what a reader asks the module for.

branchId.description: The branch the measurements were taken at.

customerId.description: The customer they are about. An identifier and nothing else: no name, no telephone number, no address.

templateId.description: The template they answer. A catalogue service type references this, never a version of it.

templateVersionId.description: The template version they were captured against, and render through forever.

versionNumber.description: Which measurement this is for that customer and template. A label a person reads, never a key.

correctsVersionId.description: The version this one corrects, or null when it is not a correction. A consumer showing a customer's history reads it to say 'superseded' rather than 'measured again'.

schemaVersion.description: The payload's major version. Agrees with the .v suffix of eventType.
